item.title: Hong Kong court quashes Jimmy Lai’s fraud conviction over Apple Daily HQ lease violation
item.description: A Hong Kong appeals court has overturned pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai‘s fraud conviction relating to an alleged lease violation at the now-shuttered Apple Daily newspaper headquarters. His jail term stemming from the case was quashed, though Lai still remains behind bars, serving 20 years in jail under a separate national security conviction. The Court […]

item.title: 8 months jail for father of wanted Hong Kong activist Anna Kwok after he tried to cancel her insurance policy
item.description: The father of a wanted Hong Kong activist has been jailed for 8 months after he sought to cancel an insurance policy linked to an “absconder.” Kwok Yin-sang appeared at West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts on Thursday morning to receive his sentence, after being found guilty earlier in February of attempting to obtain funds last year […]

item.title: Budget 2026: NGOs criticise lack of climate adaptation initiatives and support for low-income residents
item.description: International NGO Greenpeace has criticised the 2026 Hong Kong budget for lacking “people-centred climate initiatives,” as the city battles extreme weather. Meanwhile, the Society for Community Organisation (SoCO) has urged more support for low-income families. item.title: US arrests ex-Air Force pilot for training Chinese military

item.title: Booming markets propel Hong Kong exchange’s profits to record high
item.description: Hong Kong’s stock exchange reported record profits for the second consecutive year on Thursday, after the finance hub topped the global rankings for initial public offerings in 2025. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 36 percent to US$2.3 billion, while total revenue and other income jumped 30 percent to also hit a peak of US$3.7 billion. […]

item.description: Hong Kong’s justice department will consider an appeal after a court overturned pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai’s fraud conviction relating to an alleged lease violation at the now-shuttered Apple Daily newspaper headquarters. item.title: Hong Kong gov’t to recruit journalism students to intern at mainland Chinese media outlets
item.description: The Hong Kong government is set to recruit journalism students to intern at mainland Chinese media outlets, as part of a new programme to promote the understanding of China’s development among local youth. item.title: Chief Exec. John Lee appoints SCMP publisher Tammy Tam to Law Reform Commission
item.description: South China Morning Post (SCMP) publisher Tammy Tam has been appointed by Chief Executive John Lee to the Law Reform Commission (LRC). item.title: Tai Po fire: Wang Fuk Court residents could return home for belongings as early as late April, official says
item.description: A senior Hong Kong official has said authorities will arrange for residents of the seven blocks gutted in November’s Wang Fuk Court fire to return home and gather personal belongings as early as late April. item.description: Hong Kong’s finance chief has defended the government’s plan to dip into a fund that ensures the stability of its currency peg to help finance a technology hub by the city’s border with mainland China, calling the move an “investment” rather than expenditure.
